import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 562

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/562](https://www.erdosproblems.com/562)
-/

open Combinatorics Filter Real
open scoped Asymptotics

namespace Erdos562

/--
Let $R_r(n)$ denote the $r$-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number: the minimal $m$ such that if we
$2$-colour all edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $m$ vertices then there must be some
monochromatic copy of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Prove that, for $r \ge 3$,
$$ \log_{r-1} R_r(n) \asymp_r n, $$
where $\log_{r-1}$ denotes the $(r-1)$-fold iterated logarithm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_562 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (fun n ↦ log^[r - 1] (hypergraphRamsey r n)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos562

reformulations.difference: The imported definition used by erdos_562 quantifies over colourings of all finite subsets of Fin m, whereas the source colours only the r-element subsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only subsets satisfying e.card = r occur in the monochromaticity condition. Any colouring of r-element subsets extends to all finite subsets by assigning false elsewhere; conversely, any colouring of all finite subsets restricts to the r-element subsets. Both constructions preserve the possible monochromatic n-vertex sets. The predicate equivalence and equality of the resulting infima were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including degenerate sizes.

reformulations.difference: The source's positive two-sided estimate is expressed using norm-based Θ atTop on ℕ and Mathlib's totalized real logarithm.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite Ramsey's theorem ensures the defining infimum is over a nonempty set and R_r(n) ≥ n. Consequently, for each fixed r every fixed logarithm iterate tends to +∞, so the logarithms use their ordinary positive-input meaning and the final iterate is eventually positive. Thus Θ is equivalent to the existence of c_r,C_r>0 and N_r such that c_r n ≤ log^[r−1](R_r(n)) ≤ C_r n for all n≥N_r. The outer quantifier over r allows both constants and the threshold to depend on r, exactly as in asymp_r. The scratch file proves this equivalence under finite Ramsey nonemptiness; that standard existence theorem was not itself formalized in the experiment.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, A. Hajnal and R. Rado, Partition relations for cardinal numbers, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 16 (1965), 93–196, especially §3.1 and §16, pp. 139–140: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-14.pdf
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited problem, and the source still records it as OPEN. Its answer slot has type Prop and covers the entire quantified claim. Scratch checks compiled successfully: R_r(n)=n for n≤r, the r=3 logarithm is exactly log(log x), the natural-number atTop filter is nontrivial, and small finite Ramsey predicates have the expected values. The linked UCSD page has an apparent transcription error placing iterated logarithms around n rather than the Ramsey number; the reviewed file follows erdosproblems.com and agrees with EHR65 §16. Erdős Problems pages were read through Jina Reader after direct requests returned Cloudflare challenges.
